claims.text: Longitudinal spin fluctuations can be incorporated into first-principles calculations of a multicomponent high-entropy material.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations will improve the accuracy of the predicted solid-to-fluid transition temperature.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations will improve the accuracy of the predicted fusion enthalpy.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations will improve the accuracy of the predicted fusion entropy.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations will improve the accuracy of the predicted volume change at the transition.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations will improve the accuracy of the predicted dense-fluid heat capacity.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations alter energetic or free-energy contributions in high-entropy alloys.
The free-energy changes caused by longitudinal spin fluctuations alter the solid-to-fluid phase boundary.
The free-energy changes caused by longitudinal spin fluctuations alter fusion thermodynamics, transition volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
The intervention is applicable at high temperatures across various multicomponent high-entropy compositions.
The impact of longitudinal spin fluctuations on phase transitions in multicomponent systems is not well understood.
